requiredBeforeFiling.section: Why the records were created — the eight statutory grounds
requiredBeforeFiling.disclosureLabel: Ground 1 — the records were created as a result of false use of my identification (selection)
requiredBeforeFiling.why: G.L. c. 276, § 100K lists eight alternative grounds and this family's SINGLE route (obligation:track-pathway:MA:ma-expunge-k:non-time-based-expungement-for-false-identity-error-fraud-or-decriminalized-conduct-100k) spans all eight — its own name carries "false-identity-error-fraud-or-decriminalized-conduct". The route-obligation census records the waiting-period basis for this route as a record created on one of the eight statutory grounds and names none of them. Which ground created a particular participant's record is a fact of that record, held on a CORI and a court file this platform has never seen, and the judge must find it on clear and convincing evidence. Ticking one from nothing would be a legal characterisation with no record behind it, on a petition sworn under the pains and penalties of perjury.

notApplicableNote: This form has no branch this route does not use, so nothing is declared not-applicable-on-this-route. Its eight ground boxes and its four department boxes are determined by the CASE and are declared required-before-filing with that reason stated, not declared inapplicable.

participantElections.label: Continuing your explanation on the back of the sheet (selection)
participantElections.why: tick this only if you actually continue your explanation on the back of the sheet. Only you know whether you ran out of room

participantElections.label: Documents supporting the petition are attached (selection)
participantElections.why: tick this only if you are actually attaching supporting documents. The platform holds none of your documents and cannot say whether you attached any

participantElections.label: Request that the court hold a hearing on the petition (selection)
participantElections.why: whether to ask for a hearing is yours. The court's own instruction sheet on page 2 describes what a hearing is for: to tell the judge why your petition fits one of the grounds and why granting it would be in the interests of justice

participantElections.label: You gave the district attorney's office a copy by delivering it in hand (selection)
participantElections.why: tick this only after you have actually delivered a copy in hand. This sentence is a statement that you already did it, and when this packet was prepared it had not happened

participantElections.label: You gave the district attorney's office a copy by mailing it first class (selection)
participantElections.why: tick this only after you have actually posted a copy by first class mail. This sentence is a statement that you already did it, and when this packet was prepared it had not happened

participantElections.label: Request for an interpreter (selection)
participantElections.why: whether you want an interpreter is yours to decide and nobody else's. The form prints beside it that there is no charge to you for interpreter or translation services

protectedBlanks.label: The date you gave the district attorney's office a copy
protectedBlanks.why: this date certifies an act of delivery that has not happened when the packet is prepared. The form's own instruction sheet puts it on or before the day the petition is filed, which is after this build. You write the date on the day you actually deliver or post the copy

participantActsRequiredBeforeFiling.conditionDescription: Applies only when the participant cannot pay the filing fee.

whatThatFlagCovers: every form blank listed in requiredBeforeFiling and boundaryOnlyRequiredBeforeFiling, AND every participantActionRequired entry the committed packet-set manifest marks requiredBeforeFiling for this packet set -- all 7 of them, of kinds obtain_document, confirm_answer, complete_field, complete_field, sign, pay_fee, apply_fee_waiver. No entry is excluded, by kind or by anything else; participantActsExcludedFromTheFlag is empty and is generated from the same array this flag measures. A participant act counts as disclosed only when its description is a WHOLE LINE of the delivered guide, not merely a substring of one: "Required." is short enough to fall inside an unrelated sentence, and a substring test would have scored it disclosed whatever the guide printed.
howTheScopeOfThatFlagIsDerived: read at build time from data/record-clearing/legal-design-packet-set-manifests.json#packetSets[packetSetId=ma-expunge-k-set].participantActionRequired and filtered on requiredBeforeFiling === true alone. The sentence above counts the same array it measures, so this report can no longer state a different number of exclusions than it makes.
